item.title: bj-2: stack bead and sprint-family pour: stack-bead.json.j2, pour metadata, pydantic model per bead kind, validate-plan

results.statement: atm-bd must not assign dev or fix beads; the lead assigns them, the dev starts its next queued task when the sanity hook closes its current task, and a qa fix bead goes to the dev the lead picks at the finding's difficulty.
results.quote: dev assignment is not mechanical.  this works as it does now.  dev agent will start next queued task as soon as sanity pass.  a different dev will get qa fix beads at appropriate level set by lead.
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: atm-bd's actions.jsonl over a tick with a ready dev bead and no task holds no assign for it; the candidate filter in dispatch.py admits only sanity and qa stages

relevant.instructions: Consider what `item.text` would change if it were carried out. Would any of it change or rely on assigning beads to agents, atm-bd's dispatch tick and its candidate filter, or the moment a dev takes up its next queued task? These are what `anchor.statement` governs. Judge whether the subject overlaps; do not judge compliance.

criteria.no: The item leaves dev and fix assignment to the lead, or does not mention it; mechanical sanity or qa assignment alone does not count.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for a dev or fix bead to be assigned or claimed by anything other than the lead (atm-bd's dispatch, a hook or script, or the dev picking its own next bead), or for a dev to take new work other than its next queued task? Silence about dev and fix assignment is not a conflict. Mechanical assignment of sanity or qa beads is allowed by the anchor and is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.
